issues.title: Python variable uses camelCase naming
issues.description: The rule requires all Python variables and functions to use snake_case naming convention, but the code uses camelCase for the variable 'escapedPattern' instead of 'escaped_pattern'
issues.problematic_code_snippet:

issues.rule_name: Python Code Must Use Snake Case for Variables and Functions

issues.title: Missing escape parameter in 'not contains' metadata filter
issues.description: In the metadata filtering logic for dataset retrieval, the 'not contains' case applies escape_like_pattern() to escape special characters but fails to specify the escape='\' parameter in the notlike() call. This renders the escaping ineffective - the database won't interpret the backslash escapes correctly, allowing special characters like %, _, and \ to be treated as SQL wildcards instead of literal characters. This creates a SQL injection vulnerability through LIKE wildcards and causes incorrect query results when filtering metadata that contains these special characters.

issues.title: Incorrect escape character in IRIS vector database LIKE query
issues.description: The IRIS vector database implementation escapes special characters using backslash (via escape_like_pattern which produces \%, \_, \\) but then specifies ESCAPE '|' in the SQL query instead of ESCAPE '\'. This mismatch causes the database to look for the wrong escape character - it will treat | as the escape character while the string contains backslash escapes. As a result, the escaped special characters won't be properly interpreted, allowing SQL wildcards to remain active and causing search queries with special characters to produce incorrect results or security vulnerabilities.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
escaped_query = escape_like_pattern(query)
                query_pattern = f"%{escaped_query}%"
                sql = f"""
                    SELECT TOP {top_k} id, text, meta
                    FROM {self.schema}.{self.table_name}
                    WHERE text LIKE ? ESCAPE '|'
                """

issues.title: Keyword trimming logic may break escape sequences
issues.description: The workflow app service trims the keyword to 30 characters and then applies escape_like_pattern(). However, this creates a subtle bug: if a backslash character appears exactly at position 30, the trim could split an escape sequence that the user intended. More critically, if special characters appear in positions 28-30, they'll be included in the escaped output, but any context around them will be lost, potentially creating malformed escape sequences. The trimming should occur AFTER escaping to preserve the integrity of the escape sequences, or better yet, the escaping should be done before any string manipulation.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:

            escaped_keyword = escape_like_pattern(keyword_trimmed)
            keyword_like_val = f"%{escaped_keyword}%"

issues.title: Improper import ordering (isort/ruff)
issues.description: Ruff/isort requires standard-library imports to be sorted consistently. Here, `from unittest.mock ...` (module `unittest`) should be ordered before `import uuid` (module `uuid`) within the standard library import section.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30450: centralize SQL LIKE pattern escaping

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds `libs.helper.escape_like_pattern()`, which backslash-escapes `\`, `%` and `_`, and routes roughly a dozen user-keyword LIKE/ILIKE call sites through it: console conversation and segment lists, annotations, apps, datasets, external knowledge, tags, conversation variables, workflow app logs, metadata filters, and two vector-store fallbacks (IRIS and ClickZetta). Each call site now passes `escape="\\"` so the database treats the inserted backslashes as escapes. The helper itself is small and correct, and the backslash-first ordering is right and unit-tested. The framing as "SQL injection prevention" is overstated: these queries were already parameterized, so the real defect being fixed is wildcard semantics (a user's `%` or `_` acting as a wildcard).

The change has two concrete regressions and several weaker spots. The IRIS fallback pairs backslash-escaped output with `ESCAPE '|'`, so ordinary searches containing `_`, `%` or `\` return wrong results. The workflow-log keyword path drops the `unicode_escape` transform that let non-ASCII keywords match JSON stored with `\uXXXX` escapes, so CJK searches over run inputs/outputs silently stop matching. The tests add negative cases that would pass even without escaping, and cover only about four of the roughly twelve changed call sites.

Assessment: the core design is reasonable, but the two regressions need fixing before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two regressions are likely to reach users: IRIS fallback search breaks for any query containing `_`, `%` or `\`, and non-ASCII keyword search over workflow run logs stops matching stored JSON. The remaining issues (inconsistent ESCAPE clauses, an unverified ClickZetta escape literal, and weak negative tests) are worth fixing in the same pass.

architecture.overview:
User-supplied search keywords reach the database through SQLAlchemy `ilike`/`like` calls in controllers and services, and through raw SQL in a few vector-store backends (IRIS, ClickZetta). Before this PR, each call site interpolated the keyword directly into `%...%` and relied on the database's default LIKE escape rules, so `%` and `_` in user input acted as wildcards. Workflow-run keyword search had a bespoke `unicode_escape` hack to match JSON that is stored with `\uXXXX` escapes, because `json.dumps` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True`.

The PR introduces one helper, `libs/helper.py::escape_like_pattern`, that doubles backslashes and prefixes `%` and `_` with a backslash. Each caller now wraps its pattern with this helper and also has to pass a matching `escape="\\"` clause to the ORM or write an `ESCAPE` clause into raw SQL. The coupling between the helper's output and the SQL ESCAPE clause lives at every call site, not in one place, which is where the inconsistencies below come from.
steps: Entry points: console controllers (`controllers/console/app/conversation.py`, `controllers/console/datasets/datasets_segments.py`) and services (`services/app_service.py`, `dataset_service.py`, `tag_service.py`, `workflow_app_service.py`, etc.) receive a free-text keyword from the request.

New shared utility: `libs/helper.py::escape_like_pattern` escapes backslash first, then `%` and `_`. It is the single source of the escaping rule and is unit-tested in `tests/unit_tests/libs/test_helper.py`.

Call-site pattern: each ORM call becomes `column.ilike(f"%{escaped}%", escape="\\")`. Raw-SQL backends must instead carry a matching `ESCAPE` clause in the SQL text: ClickZetta writes `ESCAPE '\\'` and IRIS writes `ESCAPE '|'`.

Workflow log keyword path (`workflow_app_service.py`): the keyword is trimmed to 30 characters, then escaped. The previous `unicode_escape` conversion is removed, which changes how non-ASCII keywords match JSON-stored inputs and outputs.

Mismatch hotspots to check: the IRIS fallback (escape char differs from the one the helper emits), the metadata-filter `not contains` branch (no `escape=` argument), and the ClickZetta literal (escape string length depends on SQL dialect).

findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback uses ESCAPE '|' but the helper emits backslashes
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/rag/datasource/vdb/iris/iris_vector.py` (the LIKE fallback around lines 289-299), `escape_like_pattern` emits backslash escapes, but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`, so `_`, `%` and `\` in user queries act as wildcards or literals incorrectly. Change the ESCAPE character in that SQL to the backslash that the helper produces, keeping the parameterized `?` placeholder. Check that no other IRIS code depends on `|` as the escape. Add a test or note showing that a query containing `_` matches its literal text.

findings.title: Workflow log keyword search drops unicode_escape, breaking non-ASCII matches
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/workflow_app_service.py` (keyword block around lines 89-101), the `unicode_escape` conversion that existed on the base branch was removed. `WorkflowRun.inputs` and `outputs` are stored with `json.dumps` defaults (`ensure_ascii=True`), so non-ASCII keywords need to be matched in their `\uXXXX` form. Restore the `encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')` step on the trimmed keyword, then pass the result through `escape_like_pattern` before building `keyword_like_val`. Do not reintroduce the old `.replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` hack, because escaping now handles the backslashes. Add an integration test that searches a CJK keyword present in run inputs.

findings.title: Metadata filter `not contains` omits the ESCAPE clause
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/rag/retrieval/dataset_retrieval.py`, `process_metadata_filter_func`, the `not contains` branch (around line 1207) calls `json_field.notlike(...)` without `escape="\\"`, unlike the other three LIKE branches that were updated in the same PR. Add the same escape argument so all branches behave identically. No other behavior changes are needed.

findings.title: ClickZetta ESCAPE literal may be the wrong length for the SQL dialect
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/rag/datasource/vdb/clickzetta/clickzetta_vector.py` around lines 987-991, the LIKE clause is built with `ESCAPE '\\\\'` in an f-string. Verify against ClickZetta's SQL documentation how a single backslash escape character is written in a string literal, and make the emitted SQL match what `escape_like_pattern` produces. Do not change the `''` quote doubling. Document the verified behavior in a comment next to the clause.

findings.title: Negative assertions in new tests would pass without escaping
findings.fixPrompt: The new integration tests in `api/tests/test_containers_integration_tests/services/` (tag, annotation, app, workflow app service) claim to check that `%`/`_` are not treated as wildcards, but their negative fixtures (for example `100% different`) cannot be matched by the unescaped pattern `%50%%` in the first place, so the tests pass on the base branch. Replace each negative case with a fixture that the unescaped wildcard would match, such as `testXdata` for keyword `test_data`, and assert that it is excluded. Delete the duplicated "Test 4" blocks that repeat the earlier query. Keep the tests in the same style as the surrounding file.

findings.title: Most changed call sites have no test coverage
findings.body:
The diff changes about twelve escaping call sites, but tests cover only four services (annotation, app, tag, workflow app logs). Nothing exercises the console segment and conversation keyword filters, dataset list search, child-chunk and segment keyword search, external knowledge search, conversation-variable name search, metadata filters in `dataset_retrieval`, or the IRIS and ClickZetta vector fallbacks. The regressions above would not be caught by this test set, and the PR checklist's statement that "I've added a test for each change" does not hold.

::callout{type="info"}
Unit tests for the helper itself are good. The integration tests are the gap.

Add at least one test per changed path, prioritizing the metadata filter (four branches), the IRIS fallback, and the workflow CJK keyword case.
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests for the escaping call sites that the PR changes but does not cover. Priority: (1) the metadata filter branches in `process_metadata_filter_func` in `api/core/rag/retrieval/dataset_retrieval.py`, including `not contains`; (2) the IRIS LIKE fallback in `api/core/rag/datasource/vdb/iris/iris_vector.py`, which needs a query containing `_`; (3) the workflow keyword search with a CJK keyword in `api/services/workflow_app_service.py`. Then cover `DatasetService.get_datasets` search and the segment keyword filter in `api/controllers/console/datasets/datasets_segments.py`. Assert on returned rows, not on mock calls, and include a negative case that unescaped wildcards would match.

findings.title: Escaping contract is implicit, and every caller must pair it with an ESCAPE clause
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/libs/helper.py`, `escape_like_pattern` is paired with an `escape="\\"` argument at roughly 25 call sites across the changed services, controllers and vector stores, and the two must always match. Introduce a shared constant for the LIKE escape character, and either a helper that builds the escaped `ilike`/`like` clause or a documented pair `(pattern, escape_char)`. Migrate the changed call sites to it, keeping the existing unit tests in `api/tests/unit_tests/libs/test_helper.py` passing. Keep the helper's name and behavior stable for callers that already use it.

findings.title: Inline `libs.helper` imports repeated across many functions
findings.fixPrompt: Several services and the console conversation controller import `escape_like_pattern` inside function bodies (`api/services/app_service.py`, `tag_service.py`, `conversation_service.py`, `external_knowledge_service.py`, `annotation_service.py`, `api/controllers/console/app/conversation.py`). `api/services/dataset_service.py` already imports `libs.helper` at module level. Move these imports to the top of each module, following the existing import ordering. If a real circular import appears, keep the local import and add a comment that names the cycle.

findings.title: Unrelated test churn: AppService import moved into dozens of test bodies
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/tests/test_containers_integration_tests/services/test_app_service.py` and `test_workflow_app_service.py`, the top-level `from services.app_service import AppService` was commented out and moved into about twenty test bodies with the comment "Import here to avoid circular dependency". Restore the single top-level import, delete the commented-out line and the repeated local imports, and keep only the new test methods from this PR. Confirm the test module still imports cleanly.

findings.title: Helper docstring and naming are misleading
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/libs/helper.py` (`escape_like_pattern`, lines 35-65), clean up the docstring so it clearly states the mapping: a backslash becomes two backslashes, `%` becomes `\%`, and `_` becomes `\_`. Rename the local `escapedPattern` to `escaped_pattern` to match the file's snake_case style. Make the `None` case explicit, either by typing the parameter as `str | None` with a matching return type or by documenting it. Adjust `test_escape_none_handling` in `api/tests/unit_tests/libs/test_helper.py` to match.

findings.title: Helper escapes backslash first, and the unit tests pin that order
findings.body: The helper escapes the backslash before `%` and `_`, which avoids double-escaping the backslashes it inserts. `test_escape_order_matters` checks this with an input that mixes all three characters (`test\\%_value`). The unit tests also cover empty input, normal text, and the combined case. The `workflow_app_service.py` change trims to 30 characters before escaping, so a truncation never splits an escape sequence. That is the right order.
